body: It is a bit overkill to store these as doubles
I'm not sure if these should have a hint for the max range as the actual value depends a lot on the mass of the objects you're trying to constrain. This value can easily be >> 1000.

I'm not sure what the purpose of switching bodies is. The distance joint itself doesn't seem to mind if A or B is the static world. Won't this give problems when querying properties from the physics server where it will return the properties swapped?
Not sure if this makes sense. The transform of the joint has no meaning.

This is similar to Pin Joint -  if pin joint anchors the object to a global position and the pin joint node is moved, it will move where the global anchor is as well.
If a user anchors a node to a global position with `DistanceJoint3D` and then they move the joint, they would probably expect the global anchor to move.

This was done because Joint3D (https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/scene/3d/physics/joints/joint_3d.cpp#L101) switches the bodies as parameters. It's not necessary for Jolt, so I will ignore the parameters in `_configure_joint`
